incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: KV-cache write amplification detected for model 'long-context-v2'. sustained write rate ~4x baseline, cache footprint ~6x. suspect continuous-batching worker cb-42. Paging @Emma (oncall). root_ts=1976543210
Emma (oncall): seen it. looking at dashboard now — p99 token latency up, error spikes on kv-set (503). any known deploys?
Raj (eng-runtime): I pushed a batching config tweak ~35m ago to reduce CPU by increasing batch_window from 5ms -> 50ms for cb-workers. preliminary logs show many unique prefix keys: tokenizer mismatch + template drift?
Maria (sre): attaching sampled logs (truncated):
```
[1976543175] cb-42 batch_size=18 window_ms=50 keys=["user:123|prompt_v2:abc123", "user:124|prompt_v2:abc123 ", "user:125|prompt_v2:abc123"]
[1976543180] kv-store set key="user:124|prompt_v2:abc123 " size=2.1k
[1976543182] kv-store set key="user:124|prompt_v2:abc123" size=2.1k
[1976543185] error kv-store set slow write latency=1200ms
```
looks like trailing-space tokenizer differences are creating near-unique prefixes, combined with bigger windows we aggregate heterogeneous requests into one batch -> vastly more unique writes.
Raj (eng-runtime): yup. template rendering started including timestamps in prompt metadata after an unrelated templates PR last week — that increases cardinality. Also tokenizer update 2 deploys ago changed normalization (removed rstrip). so two factors: tokenizer normalization regression + batching window expansion.
Julie (cs): customers reporting 5xxs: ACME, BrightShop, NovaAnalytics. Julie (cs): flagged to top-5 affected, pinging account teams.
Emma (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) quick throttle kv-writes 2) revert batch_window to 5ms 3) flush noisy prefix keys for long-context-v2 4) longer-term: revert tokenizer change or normalize at cache-key layer.
Maria (sre): throttling kv-writes: running feature toggle to limit kv-set QPS from runtime layer. command: `rwdctl feature-toggle set runtime.kv_write_qps=200 --env=prod`
OpsBot: feature-toggle succeeded, runtime.kv_write_qps=200 applied to cluster runtime-prod (applied by Maria).
Raj (eng-runtime): rolling rollback of batching config now. command: `rwdctl set-config runtime continuous_batching.window_ms=5 --service=cb-workers --env=prod`
Emma (oncall): running prefix flush job for model 'long-context-v2' (targeted) — curl to ops endpoint: 
```
curl -X POST https://ops.redwood/api/v1/cache/flush \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OP_API_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"model":"long-context-v2","prefix_only":true,"pattern":"prompt_v2"}'
```
Raj (eng-runtime): started normalization hotfix (non-breaking) to reapply rstrip in cache key path and emit metric for key-cardinality. patch applied to canary, rolling to prod now.
Maria (sre): metrics update: kv-write rate down ~70% since throttle, cache size trending down, p50/p95 latency improving. customer 5xxs dropped from ~8% -> 1.2% for ACME.
Emma (oncall): current status: mitigations in place (throttle + batch rollback + targeted flush + hotfix). still watching for residual card spikes. allocating 15m for stabilization, then full handoff.
Chris (eng-platform): I'll take monitoring/watch for next 2h and lead postmortem. note to include: chain of changes (tokenizer, templates PR, batching tweak), impact window, customers affected, rollback timeline, mitigation steps, and follow-ups (fix key normalization at cache layer, add unit tests for tokenizer differences, add canary for batching window changes).
Julie (cs): I've notified all affected accounts with preliminary RCA and mitigation steps. offering credits if SLA breached.
Emma (oncall): handoff to Chris (eng-platform) at 1976543430 — leaving notes in incident ticket. next: postmortem owner=Chris, severity=SEV2, expected timeline for draft by EOD.
Chris (eng-platform): on it. creating postmortem doc and tagging eng-runtime, eng-ml, eng-sre. will also schedule a quick sync to decide long-term fix (cache-key normalization vs tokenizer rollback). :white_check_mark:
Emma (oncall): thanks team. closing page but not the incident thread — keeping it open for postmortem links. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident status updated -> MITIGATED (partial). assigned: Chris (postmortem). severity: SEV2.
